Statistics for Testing a Coefficient

Source: R/inference_objects.R
test_statistic.Rd

Four statistics test the hypothesis that one coefficient of a fit equals a value: Wald's, the likelihood ratio, Rao's score and Terrell's gradient. Each is an object built by wald_test(), lr_test(), score_test() or gradient_test(), and the object is passed as the test argument of statmod_test(), summary.StatmodFit() and confint.StatmodFit(). The default is wald_test().

test_statistic is the abstract parent of the four classes. It cannot be instantiated, and serves to test membership with S7::S7_inherits().

Usage

test_statistic(name = character(0), label = character(0))

Arguments

name

A single string, the short name of the statistic ("wald", "lr", "score" or "gradient"), which also gives the name of the constructor (wald_test() and so on).

label

A single string, the name under which a result prints the statistic (for example "Likelihood-ratio").

Value

Nothing: the class is abstract and its constructor signals an error. Every object that inherits from it has the properties name and label.

Details

Write \(\ell_p\) for the penalized log-likelihood (the log-likelihood where the model carries no penalty), \(\hat\beta\) for the estimates of the fit, \(\tilde\beta\) for the estimates in which the coefficient \(\beta_j\) is held at the tested value \(b\), \(U = \partial\ell_p\) for the penalized score and \(K\) for the penalized information. The four statistics are $$W = \frac{(\hat\beta_j - b)^2}{\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat\beta_j)}, \qquad LR = 2\{\ell_p(\hat\beta) - \ell_p(\tilde\beta)\},$$ $$S = U_j(\tilde\beta)^2\,[K(\tilde\beta)^{-1}]_{jj}, \qquad T = U_j(\tilde\beta)\,(\hat\beta_j - b),$$ and each is compared with a \(\chi^2_1\) distribution. In summary.StatmodFit() the value of a table is the signed root of the statistic, with the sign of the estimate, and the p-value is that of the \(\chi^2_1\) value.

ConstructorStatisticWhat it needsCost
wald_test()\(W\)the unrestricted fit and its variance matrixno refit
lr_test()\(LR\)the restricted refit and the objective at the unrestricted joint modeone refit per value \(b\)
score_test()\(S\)the restricted refit and its penalized informationone refit and one Hessian per value \(b\)
gradient_test()\(T\)the restricted refit and its scoreone refit per value \(b\), no matrix inversion

The three statistics that need the restricted refit are the restricted tests, and test_restricted() returns TRUE for them. The refit maximizes \(\ell_p\) over every coefficient but \(\beta_j\), at the hyperparameters of the fit, with the inner method that the fit used, and it starts from the unrestricted estimates; the outer search over the hyperparameters is not repeated. The statistics are therefore conditional on the smoothing that the data chose once. Their cost in each consumer is as follows.

  • statmod_test() runs one refit.

  • summary.StatmodFit() runs one refit per coefficient row, against zero.

  • confint.StatmodFit() inverts the statistic, which takes a few dozen refits per interval, and it requires readable = FALSE for a restricted test, because a readable quantity is a function of several coefficients at once and one coordinate cannot be held in its place.

The restricted refit is defined for a coefficient that is not under a kinked penalty (a lasso, a SCAD or an MCP), that is not aliased and that belongs to a model without a structural term. For any other coefficient the restricted statistics are NA.

The Wald statistic depends on how the coefficient is written: a nonlinear reparametrization changes it, whereas the likelihood ratio, a difference of objective values at the same two points, is not changed. It also loses power against a distant alternative (the Hauck-Donner effect), because the curvature is read at \(\hat\beta\) and not under the null. The interval that inverts the Wald statistic is symmetric about the estimate. The intervals that invert the other three follow the shape of the likelihood and are asymmetric where it is. The variance that the Wald statistic reads is set by the argument vcov_type, described at vcov_method.

See also

wald_test(), lr_test(), score_test() and gradient_test() for the four statistics, test_restricted() for the distinction between them, statmod_test(), summary.StatmodFit() and confint.StatmodFit() for the functions that take one, and vcov_method for the variance that the Wald statistic reads.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(80))
dd$y <- 1 + 2 * dd$x + rnorm(80, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)

# the four statistics of one hypothesis, that the slope is 1.5
tests <- list(wald_test(), lr_test(), score_test(), gradient_test())
vapply(tests, function(tt) {
  statmod_test(fit, param = "mu", coefname = "x", value = 1.5,
               test = tt)@statistic
}, numeric(1))
#> [1] 11.67136 11.15541 10.41256 10.41256

# which of them refit the model under the restriction
vapply(tests, test_restricted, logical(1))
#> [1] FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE

# the class itself is abstract
try(test_statistic(name = "mine", label = "Mine"))
#> Error in S7::new_object(S7::S7_object(), name = name, label = label) : 
#>   Can't construct an object from abstract class <test_statistic>
